sites.rationale: The ledger (L1–L3) uniformly describes an 'amino terminal' tag on full-length, membrane-anchored PAR3; no residue number is stated. PAR3 has a signal peptide spanning residues 1–21 (last residue S at position 21); a tag upstream of residue 22 would be cleaved with the signal peptide, so the only valid N-terminal extracellular junction is after residue 21. Python confirms seq[20]='S' and seq[21]='G', placing the tag between the last SP residue (S21) and the first mature residue (G22), 74 residues from TM1 — well clear of any TM boundary. Position is topology-derived because the paper names no residue. Full-length PAR3 with an amino-terminal HA (YPYDVPDYA) or V5 (GKPIPMPLLGLDST) epitope tag was constructed by PCR and expressed in HEK293 cells as a membrane-anchored receptor. Surface display was confirmed by antibody staining of non-permeabilized cells (Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-HA) and by flow cytometry with tag-specific antibodies.

sources.claim: An amino terminal HA (YPYDVPDYA) or V5 (GKPIPMPLLGLDST) epitope tag was added to PAR3 or PAR4 by PCR, and the cDNAs were ligated into pLUC-N2 (HA-tagged) or pGFP 2 -N2 (V5 tagged).

literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) describe the same experimental construct: an N-terminal HA or V5 tag on full-length PAR3, surface-confirmed in HEK293 cells. No other insertion sites (internal loops, C-terminus, or alternative positions) are reported in the ledger. No functional assay results (signalling, thrombin-cleavage activation) are described in the cited clips, so validation_level is surface_only. No intracellular or function-abrogating positions are mentioned in the ledger, so other_positions is empty.
